title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Calçadão. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Calçadão
options.lineage: Burle Marx's Copacabana promenade, laid in pedra portuguesa
options.thesis: Your Portuguese is a pavement you lay stone by stone: every word you learn sets a tessera in a living wave mosaic.
materials: black basalt and white limestone tesserae
options.viewport: Home opens on a full-width canvas of the wave mosaic built from your 822 words (white new, sea learning, black mastered) that ripples as you hover; beside it, today's review count and one big Start button.
options.risk: The mosaic must stay a progress display, not wallpaper; if it stops meaning your words it turns into a Rio postcard.

raised.raise: Hierarchy by scale contrast: Portuguese words at poster size, UI small, nothing in between competes.
Motion keeps identity: a graded card flies into its stone in the pavement instead of vanishing.
Each of the 8 subject groups owns one stone colour at full strength, on its tile, its cards and its part of the mosaic.
A fixed type scale as tokens no component may override; rank is weight and reversal, never ad-hoc sizes.

options.label: Azulejo Modular
options.lineage: Athos Bulcão's tile walls in Brasília
options.thesis: Every subject is a tile module; the app is a wall of them that rotates and recombines as you study.
options.viewport: A wall of square subject tiles, each with its own Bulcão-style motif; due tiles spin a quarter turn to call you, flashcards are tiles that flip.
options.risk: Blue-and-white tile is the first thing anyone pictures for Portuguese; it can read familiar and decorative.

options.label: Metro Type Tiles
options.lineage: Metro design language: flat tiles and giant lowercase
options.thesis: The words are the interface: giant lowercase Portuguese cropped off the edge, flat colour tiles that flip with live counts.
options.viewport: Black ground, 'bom dia' cropped huge off the right edge, a grid of colour tiles for Study, Practice and each subject flipping to show due counts.
options.case: Holds product clarity (tiles as subject doors, flips as cards) but loses identification: nothing about it is Brazilian.
options.risk: Reads as a 2012 phone UI when the type is not huge enough.

options.label: Full-Screen Feed
options.thesis: Review as a feed: one word owns the whole screen, actions stacked on the right, the next card one flick away.
options.viewport: One huge Portuguese word filling the screen on its subject colour, translation hidden under a tap, grade buttons on a right rail.
options.case: Strong for the daily phone review, weak for browsing topics and verb tables; identification is generic.
options.risk: Turns study into scrolling; the desk session loses structure.

options.label: Variable Type Specimen
options.thesis: Words morph on live font axes as you drag.
options.viewport: One giant word with axis sliders.
options.case: Loses both: a type foundry is not a language learner's world, and sliders are not study.
options.risk: A toy, not a study tool.

options.label: Boarding Pass & Gate Board
options.viewport: A departures board of due subjects.
options.case: Loses both: travel framing is a costume and a ranking board is not how cards are studied.
options.kept: Motion that keeps identity: things move, they do not vanish.

options.label: Acetate Tab Manual
options.thesis: Subjects as tabbed dividers under acetate leaves.
options.viewport: A stepped tab rail down the edge, one tab per subject group.
options.case: Loses both: dense and bookish, the opposite of the modern feel asked for.
options.kept: One full-strength hue per subject group.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.thesis: One type size, rank by weight and rule.
options.viewport: Raked slides of lessons on a lit bed.
options.case: Loses both: raked slides fight readability on a phone.
options.kept: A locked type scale that no component overrides.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean modern study app like the best flashcard apps, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Greeting, streak and due-count cards, a Continue button, subject cards in a grid.
canonCard.risk: Polished but forgettable: looks like every other language app.
